lens: Margaret Morse — inhabited systems (fictional analytical lens)
readerSummary: Jamie is clearly a technical project manager and implementation lead whose systems practice grows from hosting, collaborative cultural production, and civic participation. The portfolio preserves people, rooms, language, and the ability to continue together as design constraints. It does not reduce the person to organizational utility or drift into an artist biography.

evidence: The homepage names the Technical Project Manager / Product Operations & Implementation role, then pairs a facilitation photograph with a campaign interface under 'The system lives between the screen and the room.'

About's 'Systems people can inhabit' joins Open House, WOWList, Sunday Dinner and 196, NYC Artist Coalition, and Knowledge Wiki Graphs, explicitly naming artistic, civic, technical, and social practice.
The actual desktop path is Home → About; mobile is Menu → About. The current About render begins with role and implementation responsibilities before the lineage.

WOWList connects organizers' own words, followable communities, local distribution, public support, and Sunday Dinner calendars; it shares co-founder credit and states that the modern return has not restored the calendar yet.

Sunday Dinner / 196 combines a bounded shared-table photograph with two labeled reconstructions: proposal-to-independent-access and invitation-to-follow-up. Care and autonomy shape the operating steps.
FairRentNYC presents a shared campaign surface, a facilitated working session, and a collective public room as related interfaces, with sources and recollection distinguished.
The public question is whether people can 'recognize their relationships, participate, remember what happened, and continue the work.'
The residency specimen keeps the artist's direction open and makes independent access a usable result. The gathering specimen preserves welcome and minimal continuity documentation.

WOWList gives distributed organizers their own vocabulary and calendars; the coalition page connects a maintained web surface to shared decisions and follow-up. These are concrete ways to inhabit and influence a system.
About's Open House projection matches CLM-OPEN-HOUSE-PARTICIPATORY-GALLERY and attributes communal decision-making and documentation to participants.
The expanded About source note gives article author, title, date, summary, and limits; it does not reproduce the raw article or participant details.

The public-safe professor source note withholds private evaluations and the testimonial lead. No professor name, educational email, Max/Jitter reference, narrative-evaluation phrase, student ID phrase, or private absolute path matched the rendered body-text scans on ten reviewed routes.

WOWList names Richard Caceres and community contributors. FairRentNYC credits coalition collaborators and rejects solo policy causality. Sunday Dinner explicitly names Julia as a co-organizer of the 2016 milestone and keeps row-level records private.
A median across three independent judges cannot be established by this scorecard. This reader's score is 4.
